questions.q: A group of West African countries removes tariffs on goods traded among themselves and also imposes a common external tariff on goods imported from non-members. This arrangement is best described as a
options: customs union
free trade area
economic union
common market
questions.explanation: A customs union combines free trade among members with a common external tariff. A free trade area removes internal tariffs but allows each member to keep its own external tariff, while a common market also permits free movement of factors of production.

questions.q: The exchange rate of the naira changes from ₦1,450 = $1 to ₦1,600 = $1. From this change, it can be concluded that the naira has
options: appreciated against the dollar
caused the dollar to lose value against it
remained unchanged in value against the dollar
depreciated against the dollar
questions.explanation: More naira are now needed to buy one dollar, so the naira has lost value, or depreciated, against the dollar. The dollar has appreciated against the naira rather than lost value.

questions.q: A state's gross domestic product rises steadily for five years, but more pupils drop out of school and access to clean water declines. This situation best illustrates
options: sustainable economic development
balanced economic development
economic growth without economic development
economic development without economic growth
questions.explanation: Economic growth is an increase in real output, while economic development includes improvements in welfare such as education and access to clean water. Output has increased, but living conditions have worsened in those respects, so growth has occurred without development.

questions.q: The stage of development planning that involves selecting projects, estimating their costs and setting targets is known as
options: plan monitoring
plan evaluation
plan formulation
plan implementation
questions.explanation: Plan formulation is the stage where objectives are translated into projects, costs and targets. Implementation carries out the plan, evaluation compares outcomes with targets, and monitoring tracks progress during execution.

questions.q: Open market operations by the Central Bank of Nigeria are carried out mainly through the buying and selling of
options: landed property
foreign loans
treasury bills
ordinary shares
questions.explanation: Open market operations involve the central bank buying or selling short-term government securities, especially treasury bills, to influence the amount of money in circulation. Ordinary shares and landed property are not the instruments used by the Central Bank of Nigeria for this purpose.

questions.q: The Central Bank of Nigeria requires commercial banks to keep a minimum fraction of their deposits with it. This requirement is known as the
options: liquidity ratio
open market operation
bank rate
cash reserve ratio
questions.explanation: The cash reserve ratio is the proportion of deposits that commercial banks must hold with the central bank. The liquidity ratio relates to the proportion of liquid assets held by a bank, while the bank rate is the central bank’s lending rate.

questions.q: The law of diminishing returns operates in the short run mainly because
options: at least one factor of production is fixed
technology improves continuously
the firm always produces at full capacity
all factors of production are variable
questions.explanation: In the short run, additional units of a variable factor are applied to a fixed factor, so marginal returns eventually fall. If all factors were variable, the firm would be in the long run and the law would not apply in the same way.

questions.q: A firm in Ibadan produces 500 units of a good. Its total cost is ₦85,000 and its total fixed cost is ₦25,000. What is its average variable cost?
questions.explanation: Total variable cost is ₦85,000 − ₦25,000 = ₦60,000, so average variable cost is ₦60,000 ÷ 500 = ₦120. The value ₦170 is the average total cost, obtained by dividing the total cost by output without removing fixed cost.

questions.q: A tailor in Enugu produces 20 shirts at a total cost of ₦42,000. When she produces 25 shirts, her total cost becomes ₦49,500. What is the marginal cost per additional shirt between these two levels of output?
questions.explanation: Marginal cost is the change in total cost divided by the change in output: (₦49,500 − ₦42,000) ÷ (25 − 20) = ₦7,500 ÷ 5 = ₦1,500. The value ₦7,500 is the total additional cost for all five shirts, not the cost per additional shirt.

questions.q: In economics, normal profit is best described as the profit that is...
options: just sufficient to keep the entrepreneur in the business
equal to the excess of total revenue over total cost
earned when marginal revenue is greater than marginal cost
received only when total revenue exceeds explicit costs
questions.explanation: Normal profit is the minimum reward needed to keep an entrepreneur supplying entrepreneurial ability, and it is treated as part of implicit cost. It arises when total revenue just covers total economic cost, not when revenue exceeds total cost.

questions.q: Musa combines land, labour and capital to set up a tailoring business. The reward for his entrepreneurial ability is...
options: interest
rent
profit
wages
questions.explanation: The entrepreneur bears risk and organises the other factors of production, and the reward is profit. Rent rewards land, wages reward labour and interest rewards capital.

questions.q: A trader in Ilorin sells a good whose price elasticity of demand is 0.5. If he lowers the price of the good, his total revenue will most likely...
options: fall, because quantity demanded will also fall when price falls
rise, because lower prices always attract more buyers
remain unchanged, because demand is inelastic
fall, because the percentage rise in quantity demanded is smaller than the percentage fall in price
questions.explanation: With price elasticity of demand less than 1, demand is inelastic, so a fall in price causes a proportionately smaller rise in quantity demanded. The gain in sales does not offset the lower price per unit, so total revenue falls.

questions.q: When the price of a packet of biscuits is ₦40, quantity demanded is 200 packets. When the price rises to ₦50, quantity demanded falls to 160 packets. Using the arc elasticity formula, the price elasticity of demand is...
questions.explanation: Using midpoints, the percentage change in quantity is 40 ÷ 180 = 2/9, and the percentage change in price is 10 ÷ 45 = 2/9, so elasticity is 1.0. The value 0.8 comes from using the original values instead of the arc formula.

questions.q: A 10% rise in the price of butter causes the quantity demanded of margarine to rise by 6%. The cross elasticity of demand is...
options: −0.6, and the goods are complements
+1.67, and the goods are substitutes
+0.6, and the goods are substitutes
−1.67, and the goods are complements
questions.explanation: Cross elasticity is the percentage change in quantity demanded of one good divided by the percentage change in the price of another: 6% ÷ 10% = +0.6. A positive value shows that a rise in the price of butter increases demand for margarine, so the goods are substitutes.

questions.q: In a market, the demand and supply functions for yams are Qd = 100 − 2P and Qs = 20 + 3P, where price is in naira. If the government fixes the price at ₦10, what will be the quantity demanded, quantity supplied and the market situation?
options: Quantity demanded = 80 units, quantity supplied = 50 units; surplus of 30 units
Quantity demanded = 80 units, quantity supplied = 20 units; shortage of 60 units
Quantity demanded = 50 units, quantity supplied = 80 units; surplus of 30 units
Quantity demanded = 80 units, quantity supplied = 50 units; shortage of 30 units
questions.explanation: At ₦10, Qd = 100 − 2(10) = 80 units and Qs = 20 + 3(10) = 50 units. Since quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied by 80 − 50 = 30 units, there is a shortage.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a cassava-processing factory in Ogun State that buys tubers from local farmers and sells flour to bakeries?
options: An agro-based manufacturing firm that adds value to an agricultural product.
A public utility that supplies water to farmers.
A primary producer that sells unprocessed farm output.
A purely commercial firm that only transports farm produce.
questions.explanation: The factory transforms cassava tubers into flour, so it is a manufacturing activity based on an agricultural raw material. It is not primary production because the cassava has already been harvested, and it does more than transport or supply utilities.

questions.q: An all-season feeder road is built to link a farming community in Benue State with a processing town. The most likely immediate effect is that
options: the cost of transporting farm produce to the processing town falls
the quantity of farm produce supplied to the town decreases
post-harvest losses rise because produce reaches the town faster
manufacturing firms in the town reduce their purchases of raw materials
questions.explanation: A reliable feeder road lowers transport costs and makes it easier to move perishable farm produce quickly to the processing town. Easier movement normally increases, rather than reduces, the supply of raw materials reaching processors.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why agriculture and industry are considered complementary in Nigeria's development process?
options: Agriculture uses no capital, while industry uses no labour.
Both sectors produce only for export and therefore require the same imported machinery.
Agriculture supplies food and raw materials, while industry provides manufactured inputs and employment.
Both sectors compete for the same limited supply of land and cannot exchange output.
questions.explanation: The two sectors support each other because farms provide food and industrial raw materials, while industries produce tools, fertilizers, processed goods and jobs. This interdependence is weakened by claims that one sector uses no capital or that they cannot exchange output.

questions.q: Chief Eze sells a piece of land and agrees to collect payment in three instalments over six months. In this transaction, money is mainly performing the function of
options: a standard of deferred payment
a medium of exchange for immediate purchases
a store of value for holding wealth permanently
a unit of account for comparing prices of goods
questions.explanation: Money is acting as a standard of deferred payment because the parties agree now on money to be paid in the future. Immediate purchase would make it a medium of exchange, while comparing prices would make it a unit of account.

questions.q: A teacher's monthly salary rises from ₦80,000 to ₦92,000 while the consumer price index rises from 100 to 115. What happens to the teacher's real salary?
options: It remains unchanged.
It rises by 15%.
It falls by about 15%.
It rises by ₦12,000 in real terms.
questions.explanation: The initial real salary is ₦80,000 ÷ (100/100) = ₦80,000. The new real salary is ₦92,000 ÷ (115/100) = ₦80,000, so the real salary is unchanged. The nominal increase of ₦12,000 is exactly offset by the rise in the price level.

questions.q: To reduce inflation caused mainly by excess aggregate demand, the Central Bank of Nigeria is most likely to
options: raise the cash reserve ratio and sell treasury bills
reduce the policy rate and buy treasury bills
encourage commercial banks to grant more consumer loans
increase government spending on roads and bridges
questions.explanation: Raising the cash reserve ratio and selling treasury bills reduce the ability of banks to create credit, thereby reducing aggregate demand and inflationary pressure. Reducing the policy rate, buying treasury bills or encouraging more consumer loans would generally expand credit and worsen demand-pull inflation.

questions.q: A natural monopoly is most likely to arise when
options: many small firms sell identical products with no barriers to entry
average cost falls continuously over the relevant range of output, so one firm can serve the market at lower cost than many
each firm produces a differentiated product and enters freely
government grants licences to several firms to compete in the same market
questions.explanation: A natural monopoly occurs where large-scale operation is so efficient that average cost keeps falling as output expands, making a single supplier cheaper than several firms. Competition among many small firms or easy entry describes other market situations, not a natural monopoly.

questions.q: In a country with a population of 80 million, 30 million people are in the labour force and 27 million are employed. What is the unemployment rate?
questions.explanation: The number unemployed is 30 million − 27 million = 3 million. The unemployment rate is (3 million ÷ 30 million) × 100 = 10%. Dividing by total population gives 3.75%, while dividing by the employed gives about 11.1%.

questions.q: A country's population pyramid is broad at the base and narrow at the top. This structure most strongly suggests
options: a high birth rate and a relatively large young population
a high death rate among the elderly and a low birth rate
an ageing population with a small dependent young group
a stable population with equal numbers in all age groups
questions.explanation: A broad base indicates that many children have been born, producing a large young population. A narrow top shows that fewer people survive into old age, so the shape is typical of a youthful population with a high birth rate.

questions.q: A country's GDP at market prices is ₦800 billion. Net factor income from abroad is −₦20 billion, indirect taxes are ₦60 billion and subsidies are ₦20 billion. Its gross national product at factor cost is
options: ₦720 billion
₦780 billion
₦760 billion
₦740 billion
questions.explanation: GNP at market prices is ₦800 billion plus −₦20 billion, which gives ₦780 billion. GNP at factor cost is then ₦780 billion − ₦60 billion + ₦20 billion = ₦740 billion.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major problem in measuring national income in Nigeria?
options: Exclusion of intermediate goods to avoid double counting
Widespread use of market prices for all transactions
Strict record keeping by formal-sector firms
Difficulty in valuing output produced for self-consumption
questions.explanation: Output produced for self-consumption is not sold in the market, so it is difficult to value and include accurately in national income. Using market prices, excluding intermediate goods and keeping proper records are standard accounting practices rather than measurement problems.

questions.q: The interest paid by Kano State Government on a loan used to build a flyover is recorded in the state budget as
options: capital receipt
consolidated revenue
recurrent expenditure
capital expenditure
questions.explanation: Interest on a government loan is a debt-service payment and is treated as recurrent expenditure. The construction of the flyover itself is capital expenditure, while a loan received is a capital receipt.

questions.q: The Lagos State Government imposes an income tax at a constant rate of 8% on every taxable income. This tax is best described as
options: an indirect tax
a progressive tax
a regressive tax
a proportional tax
questions.explanation: A proportional tax takes the same percentage of income at all income levels. A progressive tax takes a rising proportion as income increases, while a regressive tax takes a falling proportion as income increases.

questions.q: Which of the following is an invisible export for Nigeria?
options: Insurance services provided by a Nigerian firm to a Ghanaian importer
Cocoa beans sold to a European buyer
Groundnut sold to a buyer in Niger Republic
Crude oil exported to India
questions.explanation: Invisible exports are services sold to foreigners, such as insurance services. Cocoa, crude oil and groundnut are physical goods, so they are visible exports.

questions.q: A depreciation of the naira against other currencies is likely to
options: make Nigeria's exports dearer abroad and imports cheaper at home
leave both exports and imports unchanged in naira terms
make Nigeria's exports cheaper abroad and imports dearer at home
reduce the volume of Nigeria's exports immediately
questions.explanation: When the naira depreciates, foreign buyers need fewer units of their currency to buy Nigerian goods, so exports become cheaper abroad. Imports become more expensive in naira because more naira is needed to obtain the same foreign currency.

questions.q: The main purpose of development planning in Nigeria is to
options: achieve stated economic and social objectives through coordinated policy measures
remove the need for annual government budgets
ensure that only the public sector produces goods and services
replace the price mechanism entirely in all markets
questions.explanation: Development planning coordinates public policies and resources towards stated economic and social goals. It does not abolish markets, exclude the private sector or replace annual government budgets.

questions.q: In the short-run production of a bakery in Abeokuta, the slope of the total product curve at any point gives the
options: marginal product of the variable input
average product of the variable input
total variable cost of the bakery
average fixed cost of the bakery
questions.explanation: The slope of the total product curve is the change in total output divided by the change in the variable input, which is marginal product. Average product is total product divided by the quantity of the input, not the slope of the curve.

questions.q: Which of the following can a cement factory in Ogun State vary in the short run?
options: The number of production workers employed
The size of the factory building
The installed rotary kiln
The area of land owned by the firm
questions.explanation: In the short run, at least one factor is fixed, but the firm can vary variable factors such as labour. The factory building, rotary kiln and land are typically fixed factors within that period.

questions.q: A construction firm in Abuja uses more machines and fewer workers than a similar firm in Ibadan. The firm in Abuja is said to be
options: capital-intensive
labour-intensive
capital-saving
land-intensive
questions.explanation: Capital-intensive production uses a higher proportion of capital relative to labour. A labour-intensive firm would use more workers relative to machines, while capital-saving methods use less capital per unit of output.

questions.q: A printing press in Jos has total revenue and total cost functions TR = 50Q and TC = 2,000 + 30Q, where amounts are in naira. At what output does the firm break even?
options: 200 units
100 units
50 units
40 units
questions.explanation: Break-even occurs where total revenue equals total cost: 50Q = 2,000 + 30Q, so 20Q = 2,000 and Q = 100. At 100 units, both total revenue and total cost are ₦5,000.

questions.q: A shoemaker in Aba finds that when output rises from 19 pairs to 20 pairs, marginal cost is ₦150. If total cost at 19 pairs is ₦4,000, what is total cost at 20 pairs?
questions.explanation: Marginal cost is the addition to total cost from producing one more pair, so total cost at 20 pairs is ₦4,000 + ₦150 = ₦4,150. Subtracting the marginal cost would move in the wrong direction, while ₦4,300 would add it twice.

questions.q: When the price of a loaf of bread rises from ₦800 to ₦1,000, quantity demanded at a shop falls from 300 loaves to 240 loaves. Using simple percentage changes, the price elasticity of demand is
questions.explanation: The percentage fall in quantity demanded is (300 − 240) ÷ 300 × 100 = 20%, while the percentage rise in price is (1,000 − 800) ÷ 800 × 100 = 25%. Taking the absolute value, price elasticity of demand is 20% ÷ 25% = 0.8.

questions.q: When the price of a commodity rose from ₦20 to ₦25, quantity supplied increased from 400 units to 500 units. Using the initial-value method, the price elasticity of supply is
questions.explanation: The percentage change in quantity supplied is (100 ÷ 400) × 100 = 25%, while the percentage change in price is (5 ÷ 20) × 100 = 25%. Therefore, price elasticity of supply = 25% ÷ 25% = 1.0.

questions.q: The cross elasticity of demand between bread and butter is −0.6. If the price of bread rises by 10%, the quantity of butter demanded will
options: fall by 16%
fall by 6%
fall by 0.6%
rise by 6%
questions.explanation: Cross elasticity is the percentage change in quantity demanded divided by the percentage change in the price of the related good. Thus, the change in quantity is −0.6 × 10% = −6%, meaning a 6% fall. The negative value also shows that bread and butter are complements.

questions.q: The demand for a commodity is inelastic while its supply is elastic. If a specific tax is imposed on the commodity, the greater part of the tax burden will most likely fall on
options: retailers
consumers
producers
wholesalers
questions.explanation: Tax burden falls more heavily on the side of the market that is less elastic. Since demand is inelastic and supply is elastic, consumers cannot easily reduce quantity purchased, so they bear the greater part of the tax.

questions.q: A rise in the price of beans, a close substitute for rice, will most likely cause the demand curve for rice to
options: move upward along the same curve
shift to the left
shift to the right
move downward along the same curve
questions.explanation: When beans become more expensive, some consumers switch from beans to rice, increasing the demand for rice at every price. This is a shift of the whole demand curve to the right, not a movement along the same demand curve.

questions.q: The demand and supply functions for a market are Qd = 400 − 5P and Qs = 40 + 5P. If the government fixes the price at ₦30, the quantity of excess demand or excess supply is
options: 60 units of excess demand
30 units of excess supply
60 units of excess supply
120 units of excess demand
questions.explanation: At ₦30, Qd = 400 − 5(30) = 250 and Qs = 40 + 5(30) = 190. Since quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied by 250 − 190 = 60 units, there is excess demand of 60 units.

questions.q: The land tenure system in Nigeria can discourage large-scale agricultural production mainly because it
options: makes it difficult to acquire large contiguous plots with secure title for collateral
encourages the use of too much fertilizer
forces all farmers to sell their produce to government
prevents farmers from practising crop rotation
questions.explanation: Many holdings are fragmented and titles are often insecure, making it hard for farmers to consolidate land, mechanise and use land as collateral for credit. It does not generally prevent crop rotation or force farmers to sell only to government.

questions.q: Industrial development can promote agricultural production in Nigeria mainly by
options: increasing the number of subsistence farmers
supplying improved inputs, machinery and storage facilities to farmers
encouraging farmers to abandon commercial farming
reducing the demand for agricultural raw materials
questions.explanation: Industries linked to agriculture can provide fertiliser, improved tools, processing equipment and storage facilities that raise farm productivity and reduce losses. Increasing subsistence farming or reducing demand for farm produce would not promote agricultural production.

questions.q: If a country's money supply increases by 15%, real output increases by 5% and the velocity of circulation is constant, the quantity theory of money predicts an inflation rate of
questions.explanation: Using %ΔM + %ΔV = %ΔP + %ΔY, with velocity constant, 15% = inflation + 5%. Therefore, inflation = 15% − 5% = 10%.

questions.q: A pharmaceutical company in Ogun State obtains a patent for a new malaria drug, which prevents other firms from producing the same drug. In market-structure analysis, the patent is best described as
options: a barrier to entry that can create monopoly power
a form of price discrimination
a subsidy that reduces average cost
a feature of perfect competition
questions.explanation: A patent grants exclusive production rights to the inventor, making it difficult for new firms to enter and thereby supporting monopoly power. It is not a pricing strategy, a competitive-market feature, or a cost-reducing payment by government.

questions.q: In a state in Nigeria, the crude birth rate is 42 per 1,000 and the crude death rate is 18 per 1,000. What is the annual natural rate of population increase?
questions.explanation: The natural increase is the excess of births over deaths: 42 − 18 = 24 per 1,000. Expressed as a percentage, 24/1,000 × 100 = 2.4%.

questions.q: After completing her studies at a polytechnic in Owerri, Adaobi spends five months applying for jobs before she accepts a suitable position. Her type of unemployment is best described as
options: cyclical unemployment
seasonal unemployment
frictional unemployment
structural unemployment
questions.explanation: Frictional unemployment occurs during the period between leaving one job or school and finding another suitable job. It is not caused by a mismatch in skills, seasonal work patterns, or a general fall in aggregate demand.

questions.q: Which of the following transactions is included in the calculation of Nigeria's Gross Domestic Product for the current year?
options: the payment of a pension to a retired teacher
the purchase of a newly constructed house by a civil servant in Enugu
the purchase of shares in a newly established company
the purchase of a five-year-old car from its owner
questions.explanation: GDP includes the value of newly produced final goods and services, and a newly constructed house is treated as investment expenditure. Buying shares is a financial transfer, resale of a used car adds no new production, and pensions are transfer payments.

questions.q: An employee in Ibadan has a monthly taxable income of ₦240,000. The first ₦100,000 is tax-free, and the remaining amount is taxed at 15%. His monthly income tax is
questions.explanation: Only the income above ₦100,000 is taxable: ₦240,000 − ₦100,000 = ₦140,000. The tax is 15% of ₦140,000, which is ₦21,000. Using 15% on the whole income would wrongly give ₦36,000.
